findings.title: Hard-coded CGO_ENABLED=0 can alter loaded API surface across platforms
findings.message: The check runs `go test -race` with CGO_ENABLED=1 on CI, but `childEnv()` hard-codes CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOTOOLCHAIN=local. In `go run . check` the env is passed to `packages.Load` for the root module, which may need packages to type-check from source; GOPROXY/GOSUMDB are forced to public defaults. That discards GOFLAGS, GOPROXY and GONOSUMDB, so offline or private-proxy builds can fail. More importantly, the loader's `NeedTypes|NeedDeps` without `NeedSyntax`/`NeedTypesInfo` relies on export data from the build, which with CGO disabled may silently drop cgo-only exported files. The root module may include cgo files, which would give a different API surface than the one captured on darwin/arm64.
findings.suggestion: Verify the root packages contain no cgo files. Otherwise, set the same CGO_ENABLED value used at capture time, or add a guard. Allow GOFLAGS/GOPROXY overrides for offline builds.
findings.evidence: cfg := &packages.Config{Context: ctx, Dir: root, Env: childEnv(), Mode: packages.NeedName | packages.NeedTypes | packages.NeedImports | packages.NeedDeps | packages.NeedModule}
